decisions.executionNote: Raise and gradually tilt the right gripper toward the basket; left arm stays parked. Conservative startup for joint continuity.
Advance above the rear egg while rotating toward a top-down grasp, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Lower toward the rear egg with the open gripper, completing the downward approach orientation.
Seat the fingers around the rear egg, then close fully. Retention will be checked visually after lifting.
Lift the first egg clear of the basket and begin moving toward the holder with the gripper kept closed.
The egg is visibly retained. Transfer above the holder's rear-left cup, keeping clearance and rotating to the placement approach.
Lower the retained egg toward the rear-left cup; small lateral correction. Check cup alignment before release.
Tracking slowed near the open lid. Replan from the observed pose: lift and move toward the front cup, steepening the approach to clear the lid.
Use a smaller initial correction to satisfy continuity, then retreat gently from the lid while retaining the egg.
Lower vertically over the front-left cup, away from the lid. Keep the egg closed in the gripper until it is seated.
Finish the short descent into the front-left cup and open the gripper to let the egg settle.
Withdraw upward from the released first egg, then start back toward the basket with an open gripper.
First egg is visibly in the front-left cup. Move above the basket's left remaining egg and finish a near-vertical grasp orientation.
Descend over the left egg with open fingers, using small alignment corrections and a vertical approach.
The left egg is centered between the fingers. Finish seating, close fully, and begin a small retention test lift.
Lift the second egg clear before lateral transfer, keeping the downward orientation and closed gripper.
The second egg slipped back into the basket. Reopen and realign over its shifted position for a deeper, centered grasp.
Descend vertically around the shifted left egg with open fingers; stop to inspect centering before closing.
Close around the centered egg at the current depth, then make a slow short lift to inspect retention.
The egg appears near the front of the finger pads rather than centered. Reopen, shift slightly toward it and reseat before closing again.
Lift from the reseated grasp with a gentle backward tilt and closed fingers. Watch whether the egg follows out of the basket.
The second egg is retained above the basket. Carry it over the empty front-right cup with the gripper closed.
Lower the retained egg over the front-right cup, correcting leftward alignment. Stop above seating height to inspect.
The second egg is aligned over the front-right cup. Lower the final short distance and open to release into the cup.
Two eggs are visible in the front cups. Lift clear with open fingers and start toward the remaining basket eggs.
Approach the rear of the two remaining basket eggs with the open right gripper, leaving room for a final visual alignment.
Center the rear egg in the wrist view while lowering the open fingers; inspect before closure.
The rear egg is centered between the pads. Close fully and begin a gentle lift, checking retention visually.
The egg remains in the basket after the test lift. Reopen and reseat lower and slightly toward the near side before closing again.
Lift the reseated third egg slowly with the gripper fully commanded closed; verify that it leaves the basket before transferring.
Third egg is visibly lifted. Carry it above the empty rear-right cup, preserving the grasp orientation and clearance.
The third egg slipped onto the table beside the holder. Reopen and approach its visible resting position for recovery.
The loose egg rolled toward the holder's front edge. Back off and turn the fingers to avoid the holder and basket during the recovery grasp.
Approach the loose egg from above with the fingers turned clear of the holder; lower gradually and inspect before closing.
Small centering correction and gradual closure around the loose egg. Avoid further descent against the nearby holder; test with a short lift.
The fingers closed above the loose egg rather than retaining it. Reopen and lower to its table-level height, with a small centering correction.
Depth was limited by contact. Recenter toward the egg in the wrist view without further descent, then close and test a short lift.
The jaws closed above the egg. Reopen only enough to clear it and descend gradually to the egg's sides, keeping clear of the holder.
Close at the deeper, centered position and lift slowly to check whether the loose egg is captured.
The loose egg remains beyond the fingertips. Reopen and shift outward away from the holder to center the grasp along the finger length, then approach again.
Use the improved lengthwise alignment to center the egg between the pads, close, and lift slowly without pressing farther into the table.
The loose egg is still on the table. Lift and change to a vertical approach with a narrower opening, avoiding the holder edge during the next descent.
Descend vertically above the loose egg with fingers partly open and clear of the holder. Inspect at the approach height before closing.
Center the egg lengthwise between the pads with a narrower opening to clear the holder, then close and test retention.
The egg remains below the closed tips. Reopen narrowly and lower vertically to table-level grasp height, staying clear of the holder wall.
Descent is obstructed beside the holder. Lift clear and rotate the jaw span fore-aft, so both fingers can descend beside the loose egg without spanning the holder wall.
Replan the interrupted rotation using smaller increments, continuing to lift clear of the holder before aligning the fore-aft grasp.
Finish the fore-aft jaw alignment while descending above the loose egg. This orientation should clear the holder wall.
Bring the loose egg farther between the fore-aft finger pads with a small visual centering correction and slow descent.
The egg is now between the fore-aft pads and descent is tracking. Close at this depth and make a slow test lift.
The loose egg was pushed outward rather than grasped. Reopen and reposition above its new head-camera location, now farther clear of the holder.
Contact with nearby geometry is deflecting the approach. Lift clear and narrow the fingers while rotating back toward a vertical crosswise grasp.
Finish the vertical orientation above the loose egg and descend with a modest opening, then inspect pad alignment.
The basket rim is obstructing descent. Move the gripper toward the near side and slightly left while lowering gently to clear the rim.
Descent is now unobstructed. Correct rightward toward the loose egg and lower the open pads for a centered table-level grasp.
The egg is to the right of the pads. Reopen fully and lift briefly, then recenter rightward and forward before lowering around it.
Basket contact is preventing the crosswise approach. Lift clear and rotate the jaw span fore-aft above the egg, keeping both fingers away from the basket rim.
Complete the fore-aft vertical orientation and lower over the loose egg's current position, stopping above grasp depth for alignment.
Shift left away from the basket and toward the loose egg in the wrist view before further descent; the egg is still ahead of the finger pads.
The loose egg is now centered and clear of the basket. Lower vertically with a small lengthwise correction, inspecting before closure.
The egg is too far along the finger length. Shift the open gripper outward to bring it nearer the pad centers without descending further.
Lateral motion met contact. Lift first, fully open the fingers, and recenter over the loose egg without dragging the pads along the table.
The open gripper is snagging near the holder. Narrow the jaws and withdraw straight upward before attempting another approach.
Gripper is free. Reposition above the loose egg using its head-camera location, with the jaw span fore-aft and enough opening to surround it.
Withdraw from the obstructed table recovery and approach the remaining basket egg first. Lift clear before translating and rotating.
Align over the last basket egg, completing a downward grasp orientation while descending only to inspection height.
Lower the open fingers around the remaining basket egg, with a small rightward centering correction. Inspect before closure.
The basket egg is centered between the pads. Narrow the fingers to clear the rim, close fully at grasp depth, then make a slow test lift.
The fingers closed above the egg. Reopen and lower to a deeper grasp level, correcting slightly left toward its shifted center.
The egg is beyond the near ends of the pads. Shift toward the near side at the current depth, then close around its center and test a small lift.
Test retention with a slow vertical lift, keeping the grasp orientation unchanged and the gripper closed.
The basket egg was not retained. Reopen and correct rightward and toward the near side before another controlled descent around its center.
